1| """
2| This module exports all latin and greek letters as Symbols, so you can
3| conveniently do
4| 
5|     >>> from diofant.abc import x, y
6| 
7| instead of the slightly more clunky-looking
8| 
9|     >>> x, y = symbols('x y')
10| 
11| Caveats
12| =======
13| 
14| 1. As of the time of writing this, the names ``O``, ``S``, ``I``, ``N``,
15|    ``E``, and ``Q`` are colliding with names defined in Diofant. If you import
16|    them from both ``diofant.abc`` and ``diofant``, the second import will "win".
17|    This is an issue only for * imports, which should only be used for
18|    short-lived code such as interactive sessions and throwaway scripts that do
19|    not survive until the next Diofant upgrade, where ``diofant`` may contain a
20|    different set of names.
21| 
22| 2. This module does not define symbol names on demand, i.e.
23|    ``from diofant.abc import foo`` will be reported as an error because
24|    ``diofant.abc`` does not contain the name ``foo``. To get a symbol named
25|    `'foo'`, you still need to use ``Symbol('foo')`` or ``symbols('foo')``.
26|    You can freely mix usage of ``diofant.abc`` and ``Symbol``/``symbols``, though
27|    sticking with one and only one way to get the symbols does tend to make the
28|    code more readable.
29| """
30| 
31| import string
32| 
33| from .core import Symbol, symbols
34| from .core.alphabets import greeks
35| 
36| 
37| # ##### Symbol definitions #####
38| 
39| a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h, i, j, k, l, m = symbols('a:m')
40| n, o, p, q, r, s, t, u, v, w, x, y, z = symbols('n:z')
41| 
42| A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, I, J, K, L, M = symbols('A:M')
43| N, O, P, Q, R, S, T, U, V, W, X, Y, Z = symbols('N:Z')
44| 
45| alpha, beta, gamma, delta = symbols('alpha, beta, gamma, delta')
46| epsilon, zeta, eta, theta = symbols('epsilon, zeta, eta, theta')
47| iota, kappa, lamda, mu = symbols('iota, kappa, lamda, mu')
48| nu, xi, omicron, pi = symbols('nu, xi, omicron, pi')
49| rho, sigma, tau, upsilon = symbols('rho, sigma, tau, upsilon')
50| phi, chi, psi, omega = symbols('phi, chi, psi, omega')
51| 
52| 
53| # ##### Clashing-symbols diagnostics #####
54| 
55| # We want to know which names in Diofant collide with those in here.
56| # This is mostly for diagnosing Diofant's namespace during Diofant development.
57| 
58| _latin = list(string.ascii_letters)
59| # OSINEQ should not be imported as they clash; gamma, pi and zeta clash, too
60| _greek = list(greeks)  # make a copy, so we can mutate it
61| # Note: We import lamda since lambda is a reserved keyword in Python
62| _greek.remove('lambda')
63| _greek.append('lamda')
64| 
65| 
66| def clashing():
67|     """Return the clashing-symbols dictionaries.
68| 
69|     ``clash1`` defines all the single letter variables that clash with
70|     Diofant objects; ``clash2`` defines the multi-letter clashing symbols;
71|     and ``clash`` is the union of both. These can be passed for ``locals``
72|     during sympification if one desires Symbols rather than the non-Symbol
73|     objects for those names.
74| 
75|     Examples
76|     ========
77| 
78|     >>> from diofant.abc import _clash1, _clash2, _clash
79|     >>> sympify('Q & C', locals=_clash1)
80|     And(C, Q)
81|     >>> sympify('pi(x)', locals=_clash2)
82|     pi(x)
83|     >>> sympify('pi(C, Q)', locals=_clash)
84|     pi(C, Q)
85| 
86|     Note: if changes are made to the docstring examples they can only
87|     be tested after removing "clashing" from the list of deleted items
88|     at the bottom of this file which removes this function from the
89|     namespace.
90| 
91|     """
92|     ns = {}
93|     exec('from diofant import *', ns)  # pylint: disable=exec-used
94|     clash1 = {}
95|     clash2 = {}
96|     while ns:
97|         k, _ = ns.popitem()
98|         if k in _greek:
99|             clash2[k] = Symbol(k)
100|             _greek.remove(k)
101|         elif k in _latin:
102|             clash1[k] = Symbol(k)
103|             _latin.remove(k)
104|     clash = {}
105|     clash.update(clash1)
106|     clash.update(clash2)
107|     return clash1, clash2, clash
108| 
109| 
110| _clash1, _clash2, _clash = clashing()
111| 
112| del _latin, _greek, clashing, greeks, symbols, Symbol

1| from itertools import combinations_with_replacement
2| 
3| from ..core import Derivative, Eq, Function, Symbol, diff, sympify
4| from ..core.compatibility import iterable
5| 
6| 
7| def euler_equations(L, funcs=(), vars=()):
8|     r"""
9|     Find the Euler-Lagrange equations for a given Lagrangian.
10| 
11|     Parameters
12|     ==========
13| 
14|     L : Expr
15|         The Lagrangian that should be a function of the functions listed
16|         in the second argument and their derivatives.
17| 
18|         For example, in the case of two functions `f(x,y)`, `g(x,y)` and
19|         two independent variables `x`, `y` the Lagrangian would have the form:
20| 
21|             .. math:: L\left(f(x,y),g(x,y),\frac{\partial f(x,y)}{\partial x},
22|                       \frac{\partial f(x,y)}{\partial y},
23|                       \frac{\partial g(x,y)}{\partial x},
24|                       \frac{\partial g(x,y)}{\partial y},x,y\right)
25| 
26|         In many cases it is not necessary to provide anything, except the
27|         Lagrangian, it will be auto-detected (and an error raised if this
28|         couldn't be done).
29| 
30|     funcs : Function or an iterable of Functions
31|         The functions that the Lagrangian depends on. The Euler equations
32|         are differential equations for each of these functions.
33| 
34|     vars : Symbol or an iterable of Symbols
35|         The Symbols that are the independent variables of the functions.
36| 
37|     Returns
38|     =======
39| 
40|     eqns : list of Eq
41|         The list of differential equations, one for each function.
42| 
43|     Examples
44|     ========
45| 
46|     >>> L = (f(t).diff(t))**2/2 - f(t)**2/2
47|     >>> euler_equations(L, f(t), t)
48|     [Eq(-f(t) - Derivative(f(t), t, t), 0)]
49|     >>> L = (f(t, x).diff(t))**2/2 - (f(t, x).diff(x))**2/2
50|     >>> euler_equations(L, f(t, x), [t, x])
51|     [Eq(-Derivative(f(t, x), t, t) + Derivative(f(t, x), x, x), 0)]
52| 
53|     References
54|     ==========
55| 
56|     * https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euler%E2%80%93Lagrange_equation
57| 
58|     """
59|     L = sympify(L)
60|     funcs = tuple(funcs) if iterable(funcs) else (funcs,)
61| 
62|     if not funcs:
63|         funcs = tuple(L.atoms(Function))
64|     else:
65|         for f in funcs:
66|             if not isinstance(f, Function):
67|                 raise TypeError(f'Function expected, got: {f}')
68| 
69|     vars = tuple(vars) if iterable(vars) else (vars,)
70| 
71|     if not vars:
72|         vars = funcs[0].args
73|     else:
74|         vars = tuple(sympify(var) for var in vars)
75| 
76|     if not all(isinstance(v, Symbol) for v in vars):
77|         raise TypeError(f'Variables are not symbols, got {vars}')
78| 
79|     for f in funcs:
80|         if not vars == f.args:
81|             raise ValueError(f"Variables {vars} don't match args: {f}")
82| 
83|     order = max(len(d.variables) for d in L.atoms(Derivative)
84|                 if d.expr in funcs)
85| 
86|     eqns = []
87|     for f in funcs:
88|         eq = diff(L, f)
89|         for i in range(1, order + 1):
90|             for p in combinations_with_replacement(vars, i):
91|                 eq += (-1)**i * diff(L, diff(f, *p), *p)
92|         eqns.append(Eq(eq, 0))
93| 
94|     return eqns

2| from ..core.compatibility import is_sequence

16| def minimize(f, *v):
17|     """Minimizes `f` with respect to given variables `v`.
18| 
19|     Examples
20|     ========
21| 
22|     >>> minimize(x**2, x)
23|     (0, {x: 0})
24| 
25|     >>> minimize([x**2, x >= 1], x)
26|     (1, {x: 1})
27|     >>> minimize([-x**2, x >= -2, x <= 1], x)
28|     (-4, {x: -2})
29| 
30|     See Also
31|     ========
32| 
33|     maximize
34| 
35|     """
36|     f = set(map(sympify, f if is_sequence(f) else [f]))
37| 
38|     constraints = {c for c in f if c.is_Relational}
39| 
40|     assert len(f - constraints) == 1
41| 
42|     obj = (f - constraints).pop()
43| 
44|     if not v:
45|         v = obj.free_symbols
46|         if not v:
47|             return obj, {}
48|     v = list(ordered(v))
49|     dim = len(v)
50| 
51|     assert all(x.is_Symbol for x in v)
52| 
53|     constraints = canonicalize_inequalities(constraints)
54| 
55|     if dim == 1:
56|         x = v[0]
57|         if constraints:
58|             constraints.extend([x - oo < 0, -oo - x < 0])
59|             dom = reduce_inequalities(constraints, x).as_set()
60|         else:
61|             dom = Interval(-oo, oo, True, True)**len(v)
62|         return minimize_univariate(obj, x, dom)
63| 
64|     polys = [obj.as_poly(*v)] + [c.lhs.as_poly(*v) for c in constraints]
65|     is_polynomial = all(p is not None for p in polys)
66|     is_linear = is_polynomial and all(p.is_linear for p in polys)
67| 
68|     if is_linear:
69|         # Quick exit for strict forms
70|         if any(isinstance(c, Lt) for c in constraints):
71|             return
72| 
73|         # Transform to the standard form: maximize cᵀx with m⋅x≤b, x≥0.
74|         # We replace original vector of unrestricted variables v with
75|         # x of doubled size, so e.g. for the first component of v we
76|         # will have v₁ = x₁⁺ - x₁⁻, where x₁⁺≥0 and x₁⁻≥0.
77|         c = [-polys[0].coeff_monomial(x) for x in v]
78|         c.extend([-_ for _ in c])
79|         m = [([+p.coeff_monomial(x) for x in v] +
80|               [-p.coeff_monomial(x) for x in v])
81|              for p in polys[1:]]
82|         b = [-p.coeff_monomial(1) for p in polys[1:]]
83| 
84|         res, sol = simplex(c, m, b)
85|         res -= polys[0].coeff_monomial(1)
86|         sol = map(lambda x, y: x - y, sol[:dim], sol[dim:])
87| 
88|         return -res, dict(zip(v, sol))
89| 
90|     raise NotImplementedError

93| def maximize(f, *v):
94|     """
95|     Maximizes `f` with respect to given variables `v`.
96| 
97|     See Also
98|     ========
99| 
100|     minimize
101| 
102|     """
103|     f = set(map(sympify, f if is_sequence(f) else [f]))
104| 
105|     fv, d = minimize([e if e.is_Relational else -e for e in f], *v)
106|     return -fv, d
107| 
108| 
109| def minimize_univariate(f, x, dom):
110|     extr = {}
111| 
112|     if dom.is_Union:
113|         for d in dom.args:
114|             fp, r = minimize_univariate(f, x, d)
115|             extr[r[x]] = fp
116|     elif dom.is_Interval:
117|         if not dom.left_open:
118|             extr[dom.start] = limit(f, x, dom.start)
119|         if not dom.right_open:
120|             extr[dom.end] = limit(f, x, dom.end, dir='-')
121|         for s in singularities(f, x):
122|             if s in dom:
123|                 m = Min(limit(f, x, s), limit(f, x, s, dir='-'))
124|                 if m == -oo:
125|                     return -oo, dict({x: s})
126|                 else:
127|                     extr[s] = m
128| 
129|         for p in solve(diff(f, x), x):
130|             p = p[x]
131|             if p in dom:
132|                 extr[p] = f.subs({x: p})
133|     elif dom.is_FiniteSet:
134|         for p in dom.args:
135|             extr[p] = f.subs({x: p})
136|     else:
137|         raise NotImplementedError
138| 
139|     if extr:
140|         min, point = oo, nan
141|         for p, fp in sorted(extr.items()):
142|             if fp < min:
143|                 point, min = p, fp
144|         return min, dict({x: point})

151| def simplex(c, m, b):
152|     """
153|     Simplex algorithm for linear programming.
154| 
155|     Find a vector x with nonnegative elements, that maximizes
156|     quantity `c^T x`, subject to the constraints `m x <= b`.
157| 
158|     Examples
159|     ========
160| 
161|     >>> simplex([2, 3, 4], [[3, 2, 1], [2, 5, 3]], [10, 15])
162|     (20, (0, 0, 5))
163| 
164|     References
